questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Inverse Laplace Transform of a Function Using the Scalar Multiplication Property
questions.worked_solution:
From the table of Laplace transforms, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{t}^{3}} & =\frac{3!}{{s}^{3+1}}=\frac{6}{{s}^{4}},\,s>0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by applying the inverse Laplace transform to the above result, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{t}^{3}} & =\frac{6}{{s}^{4}} \\ {L}^{-1}{L{{t}^{3}}} & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{6}{{s}^{4}}} \\ {t}^{3} & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{6}{{s}^{4}}} \\ {L}^{-1}{\frac{6}{{s}^{4}}} & ={t}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the multiplicative property of the inverse Laplace transform, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}6\cdot {L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{{s}^{4}}}={t}^{3} \\ {L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{{s}^{4}}}=\frac{1}{6}{t}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the inverse Laplace transform for $F(s)=\frac{4s}{{s}^{2}+9}.$
questions.worked_solution:
From the table of Laplace transforms, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L{\operatorname{cos}⁡3t} & =\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+{3}^{2}}=\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+9},\,s>0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by applying the inverse Laplace transform to the above result, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L{\operatorname{cos}⁡3t} & =\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+9} \\ {L}^{-1}{L{\operatorname{cos}⁡3t}} & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+9}} \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡3t & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+9}} \\ {L}^{-1}{\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+9}} & =\operatorname{cos}⁡3t.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the multiplicative property of the inverse Laplace transform, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}4\cdot {L}^{-1}{\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+9}}=4\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡3t \\ {L}^{-1}{\frac{4s}{{s}^{2}+9}}=4\operatorname{cos}⁡3t.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Inverse Laplace Transform of a Function Using the Addition Property
questions.worked_solution:
We decompose the fraction into a sum of partial fractions, as follows:

$$
\frac{s-2}{{s}^{2}}=\frac{1}{s}-\frac{2}{{s}^{2}}
$$

From the table of Laplace transforms, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L{1} & =\frac{1}{s},\,s>0, \\ L{t} & =\frac{1}{{s}^{2}},\,s>0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the addition and multiplication properties of the inverse Laplace transform, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s}-\frac{2}{{s}^{2}}} & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s}}-2{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{{s}^{2}}} \\  & =1-2t.\end{aligned}
$$

So the inverse Laplace transform of $F(s)=\frac{s-2}{{s}^{2}}$ is $f(t)=1-2t.$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Inverse Laplace Transform Using Partial Fractions
questions.worked_solution:
First, we write $F(s)$ as a sum of partial fractions, as follows: 

$$
\frac{2}{{s}^{2}-1}=\frac{2}{(s-1)(s+1)}=\frac{1}{s-1}-\frac{1}{s+1}
$$

From the table of Laplace transforms, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{e}^{t}} & =\frac{1}{s-1},\,s>1 \\ L{{e}^{-t}} & =\frac{1}{s+1},\,s>-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the addition property of the Laplace transform, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s-1}-\frac{1}{s+1}} & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s-1}}-{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s+1}} \\  & ={e}^{t}-{e}^{-t}.\end{aligned}
$$

So the inverse Laplace transform of $F(s)=\frac{2}{{s}^{2}-1}$ is $f(t)={e}^{t}-{e}^{-t}.$

questions.problem: Find the inverse Laplace transform for $F(s)=\frac{8}{{s}^{2}-16}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we write $F(s)$ as a sum of partial fractions, as follows: 

$$
\frac{8}{{s}^{2}-16}=\frac{8}{(s-4)(s+4)}=\frac{1}{s-4}-\frac{1}{s+4}
$$

From the table of Laplace transforms, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{e}^{4t}} & =\frac{1}{s-4},\,s>4 \\ L{{e}^{-4t}} & =\frac{1}{s+4},\,s>-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the addition property of the Laplace transform, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s-4}-\frac{1}{s+4}} & ={L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s-4}}-{L}^{-1}{\frac{1}{s+4}} \\  & ={e}^{4t}-{e}^{-4t}.\end{aligned}
$$

So the inverse Laplace transform of $F(s)=\frac{8}{{s}^{2}-16}$ is $f(t)={e}^{4t}-{e}^{-4t}.$
